requires: libsystem_sandbox.sandbox_check(pid, NULL, 0) == 0 -- the process must NOT be sandboxed
the ancestry walk must reach pid 1 AND include a process whose executable path ENDS WITH '/Terminal'
THE_GATE.which_condition_failed: Only the third. The rejection was TOP_LEVEL_TERMINAL_REQUIRED, which is raised after the sandbox and nested-codex checks have already passed.
THE_GATE.purpose: A deliberate integrity control: Route A refuses to run except as a genuine top-level local process launched from macOS Terminal.app. It exists precisely to stop nested or agent-driven execution.

why_it_fails: The chain terminates at iTermServer-3.6.11. No element ends with '/Terminal'.
IMPORTANT: This is NOT specific to the agent. Route A cannot be launched from iTerm2 by anyone, because iTerm2's session server is named iTermServer-<version>. It requires macOS Terminal.app specifically.

circumvention_considered_and_REFUSED: Faking /bin/ps output or spoofing the ancestry
Re-parenting the process to appear top-level
DISPOSITION.reason: Every one of these defeats a deliberate integrity control and would invalidate Route A as benchmark evidence. The gate is doing exactly what it was written to do; the correct response is to satisfy it, not to disable it.
DISPOSITION.legitimate_path: The operator launches Route A from macOS Terminal.app.
DISPOSITION.handover: TREE/RUN_ROUTE_A_FROM_TERMINAL.command (executable; supports --reset to archive spent claim/budget state before a retry).

PREFLIGHT_LESSON.gap: My pre-dispatch audit covered write-target collisions and authorization keys, but NOT runtime environment preconditions on the post-claim path.
PREFLIGHT_LESSON.was_it_catchable: YES, for free. top_level() is read-only and could have been called offline before dispatch. Three facets are needed, not two: (1) write targets, (2) input keys, (3) runtime preconditions -- all enumerated FROM THE SOURCE on the path after the one-shot claim.
